newsitem.title: JAPAN: Profits soar at Japan's Daihatsu on RV boom.
newsitem.headline: Profits soar at Japan's Daihatsu on RV boom.

text.p: A boom in recreational vehicles sent profits soaring at Japan's Daihatsu Motor Co. Ltd. in the first half of the fiscal year, as motorists snapped up the firm's nifty little cars, the company said Thursday.
Daihatsu, Japan's second biggest minicar maker, said its profits more than doubled in the six months ending in September, rising a steep 130 percent.

Daihatsu, 33.4 percent owned by Toyota Motor Corp., unveiled a parent company current profit of 5.18 billion yen ($46.2 million) for the six months ending in September compared with 2.29 billion ($20.4 million) a year earlier.

The company revised upward its profit forecast for the full year to 13 billion yen ($116 million) from its May forecast of 11 billion yen ($98.2 million) and against an actual 9.77 billion yen ($87.2 million) profit the year before. This would be its fourth rise in annual profits in a row.
Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains and losses on securities investments and other non-operating activities.
